fdroid:com.craxiom.networksurvey.name: Network Survey
fdroid:com.craxiom.networksurvey.summary: Survey cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GNSS, then log, stream or upload the data
fdroid:com.craxiom.networksurvey.description:
Network Survey turns an Android phone into a wireless survey tool. Pick what to survey, pick where the data goes, and press Start survey. One survey, one Start and one Stop.
 What it records 
 Cellular: serving and neighbor cells for GSM, CDMA, UMTS, LTE and 5G NR, including carrier aggregation
 Phone state: what the radio is doing
 Wi-Fi: access points, with channel, security and 802.11 standard
 Bluetooth: Classic and BLE devices, with company names and Find My trackers
 GNSS: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS, IRNSS and SBAS satellites
 Call records: calls, texts (SMS and MMS) and cell tower changes, saved to log files
 Where the data goes 
 Turn on one destination or several at once:
 Log files: CSV files on the phone
 NS Analytics: uploads to your team's workspace
 MQTT stream: JSON records to your own broker (for example Mosquitto ), with TLS and QR code setup
 gRPC stream: records to your own gRPC server
 Community databases: OpenCelliD and BeaconDB
 Message formats: messaging.networksurvey.app 
 NS Analytics 
 NS Analytics is the web analytics companion for Network Survey data. Connected phones upload their records to your workspace, so nobody copies files off phones. See your surveys on one map, open an analysis page for each record type, and export the raw records. Connect a phone by scanning the QR code on your workspace's Devices page. It is a separate web service: networksurvey.app/analytics 
 And more 
 Signals: live Cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GNSS views, including AGC and C/N0 trends
 Map: towers from OpenCelliD and BTSearch, and the points your NS Analytics and Community database surveys covered, colored by signal strength
 Watchlist alerts when a saved Wi-Fi network is seen
 Cellular tools, PLMN lookup, OUI lookup and Wi-Fi spectrum
 Saved setups, light and dark themes, and nine accent colors
 Managed configuration (MDM) per record type and destination, and an Intent API
 Permissions and privacy 
 Location is needed because every record needs a position, and Android requires it to scan Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Background location is requested only if you turn on Start survey automatically. This build has no Firebase, analytics or crash reporting. Privacy policy 
 Some anti-malware apps flag Network Survey because it can read SMS. It never sends texts and installs nothing. The SMS and call log permissions are used only for Call records (text events and the other party's number) and are asked for only when you turn Call records on, or set a survey that records them to start automatically. Both are optional: without them Call records still logs calls and tower changes. More on GitHub 
 Open source (Apache 2.0): github.com/christianrowlands/android-network-survey . Manual: networksurvey.app/manual . Requires Android 8.0 or later.

fdroid:com.noirdraco.pixelcomfort.name: PixelComfort
fdroid:com.noirdraco.pixelcomfort.summary: Comfort View off in the camera, private DNS by Wi‑Fi, AOD rules and more
fdroid:com.noirdraco.pixelcomfort.description:
The comfort filter on Google Pixel ("Comfort View", Settings → Display & touch → Comfort filters) gives the display a warmer, pastel look. That is easy on the eyes but bad for taking photos: the viewfinder and the Photos preview get a colour cast. Unlike Night Light, Google offers no schedule and no API for it.
PixelComfort turns Comfort View off as soon as you open the camera or Google Photos and restores exactly the previous state when you leave. If the filter was off before, it stays off. Other settings (dynamic, intensity) are never touched.
Around that, PixelComfort bundles a few more small automations for your Pixel. Each one has its own card on the home screen and can be switched on separately.
 Features 
 Comfort View: pauses it in the apps you pick and restores it afterwards; main switch and Quick Settings tile to switch it by hand
 Private DNS by Wi‑Fi: off on your home Wi‑Fi (so e.g. AdGuard Home filters), on everywhere else
 Hide the mobile signal icon while Wi‑Fi is connected
 Auto-rotate only in the apps you choose, with a Quick Settings tile
 Always-on display by Bluetooth device or Wi‑Fi, e.g. off in the car
 Quick Settings tile for NFC
 Sliders for display size and font size, with plus/minus for fine steps and a Default button each
 App picker with icons and search
 History of what was paused, restored or switched, and what went wrong
 Notification when Shizuku isn't running
 Material You, light and dark, English and German
 Requirements 
 Android 13 or newer. Comfort View needs a Google Pixel with the comfort filter (Android 17, Pixel Drop March 2026 or later). Tested on a Pixel 10 Pro with Android 17.
 Shizuku installed and running – the Comfort View setting is locked for normal apps. Display size also uses Shizuku; most other features only need permissions that the app grants itself once via Shizuku.
 The app's accessibility service turned on. It only listens for which app is in the foreground and does not read screen content.
The location permission is only needed for Wi‑Fi rules (private DNS, always-on display), because Android reveals the Wi‑Fi name only to apps with location access. The Bluetooth permission is only used to notice which device connects; the app never scans. No data leaves the device; the app has no internet permission.
Use at your own risk: the app changes system settings. Not an official Google product. "Pixel" is a trademark of Google LLC.

fdroid:com.wattwurm.toodoo.name: toodoo
fdroid:com.wattwurm.toodoo.summary: toodoo - a minimalistc task manager, just tasks, categories, filtering, sorting
fdroid:com.wattwurm.toodoo.description:
Features of toodoo
 Tasks: 
You can create, change and delete tasks.
Each task has a name, a category, a priority (HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW), and a completion-status (i.e. it is either OPEN or DONE).
Optionally, each task can also have a description (arbitrary text), a due_date and a due_time.
In order to avoid unintentional deletion, a task can only be deleted if it is DONE.
 Categories: 
You can create as many categories as you need.
The category a task belongs to can be changed.
A category can be renamed. This will affect all tasks that belong to that category.
Unused categories can be deleted. I.e. deletion is only possible if the category has no tasks, and if it is not used in the current filter.
 Filtering tasks: 
It is possible to restrict the tasks displayed in the list, e.g. completed tasks only, or tasks with low priority only, etc.
In general, the tasks to be displayed in the list can be filtered by
* completion_status
* due_date/due_time
* priority
* category
or any combination of these.
For due_date there are several predefined filter options, e.g. TODAY, CURRENT_WEEK, OVERDUE, TASKS_WITHOUT_DATE, etc.
For priority and category, it is possible to filter with more than one option. E.g. you can choose to show tasks with priorities HIGH or MEDIUM. Or you can display all tasks that have either category "Family" or "Friends".
 Sorting tasks: 
The task list can be sorted by:
* completion_status
* due_date/due_time
* priority
* category
* name
Any sort order is possible. E.g. first by due_date/time, then by completion status, category, priority and name. Or any other order you prefer.
 Searching tasks: 
Tasks can be searched by text. The search text you enter can be applied to the task name, the task description, or both.
Case-sensitive search is possible.
In the list of search results, when displaying details of a task, the search string is highlighted in the task name and / or description.
 Convenience: 
There are shortcuts for often used actions. E.g.
* From the context menu of a category you can jump to a list of all tasks for that category.
* From the context menu of a task you can change its completion_status, set it to DONE (or OPEN respectively), or set its due date to today or tomorrow.
* When the task list is filtered by "tasks due TODAY", you can easily move to the previous / next day by swiping right / left.
* Similarly, by swiping you can easily move to the previous / next week (when the task list is filtered by "tasks due CURRENT_WEEK"), or to the previous / next category (when all tasks for a category are displayed).
 Display: 
Tasks due in the past, today, or in the future have different background colors, so they are easily discernible.
The color scheme adapts to the display mode of the underlying android. I.e. if dark mode is selected (provided your android does support dark mode), a dark color scheme is used also for toodoo.
 Import / Export: 
All user data (i.e. tasks, categories, filters and sort criteria) can be exported to an external file (xml-format).
Vice versa, data can be imported from an external file.
 Technical: 
Your data is stored locally on your device.
No connection to the internet needed.
No ads. No tracking.
 Restrictions 
toodoo is minimalistic. It focuses on managing, categorizing, filtering, and sorting tasks (however, more features may be added in future releases.)
Thus, there are some restriction, i.e.:
* The user interface is in English only.
* Name of folder and file for export data are fixed (i.e. /Download/toodoo/toodooData-yyyy-mm-dd-hh-mm-ss)
* Settings are currently fixed, e.g.
- date format is yyyy-mm-dd, time format is 24 hours.
- first day of week is Monday.
- within a day, tasks without due_time are sorted behind tasks with due_time.

flathub:com.vargary.focal.summary: Organize tasks & notes in a tree.
flathub:com.vargary.focal.description:
Tired of scattered notes and lost tasks? Focal brings everything together in one place. Organize
 your ideas, projects, and to-dos in a simple outline format—like folders within folders—so you
 can always find what you need.
 🌳 Outline Your Way: Nest notes inside notes, just like an outline. Break big projects into smaller
 pieces and keep related items together.

 visually with kanban boards. Use what works for you.
 🔍 Find Anything Fast: Search across all your notes and tasks instantly. Create smart lists that
 automatically gather items by tag, status, or date.

 Filter by tag to see exactly what you need.
 ✏️ Write Your Way: Use simple text or rich formatting with headings, lists, and styling—whatever
 suits your style.
 ☁️ Sync Everywhere: Access your notes on all your devices. Everything stays backed up and in

 and rich set of features.
 Features include: 
 Free & open-source (licensed under GPLv3)
 Cross-platform (Linux, OS X, Chrome OS, and Windows)
 Easy-to-use user interface (designed for beginners, built-in tutorial)

 Audio mixing, waveform, & editing

 Credits & captions (scrolling and animated)
 Hardware accelerated (encoding & decoding supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and more)
 Import & export (EDL and Final Cut Pro formats, supports most video editors)
 Customizable keyboard shortcuts 
 Translations (available in 100+ languages)

firefox-addons:2938270.name: WordGlance - Dictionary & Translation
firefox-addons:2938270.summary: Get instant dictionary definitions and translations for any text on any website! Just select text and click the book icon.
firefox-addons:2938270.description:
WordGlance - Your instant dictionary and translation companion!
 ✨ What it does: 
 Dictionary : Get definitions, examples, synonyms, and antonyms instantly
 Pronunciation : Hear words read aloud with one tap, when audio is available
 Translation : See the word's equivalents in your target language, with several to choose between
 Per-site control : Turn WordGlance off on individual websites, right from the popup
 Mobile-friendly : Works perfectly on both desktop and mobile
 Customizable : Choose your preferred languages and settings
 How to use: 
 Select a single word on any website
 Click the 📖 icon that appears
 Get instant definitions and translations
 Click the ‹ › arrows to browse multiple results
A Lookup is about one word. The 📖 icon appears for a single word — WordGlance
does not translate a sentence, a phrase, or a passage. It shows that word's
equivalents in your target language, so you can pick the formal or the colloquial
one.
 Target languages — the language you want a word's equivalents in. Coverage
depends on the source, because each pair comes from a different source: Wiktionary
where it has a Translations block, and a machine-translation fallback where it
does not, which is rougher and usually offers one word rather than several.
Amharic, Arabic, Bengali, Bulgarian, Chinese, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Filipino, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Malay, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Zulu
 Definitions are English-first. They come from a dictionary of the 19,555
commonest English words that ships inside the extension, and for other languages
from a live provider whose coverage we have measured for one language and not for
the rest. If you read in a language we have not measured, treat the quality as
unverified rather than good.
 Features: 
 Choose the language you are reading in, or leave it on auto-detect
 Customizable target language (defaults to English)
 Dark mode toggle
 Smart caching system
 Works on all websites (or turn it off per-site)
 No account required
 Completely free and open source
 Privacy & Security: 
 The word you select is sent straight from your browser to the services below — that is the only data that ever leaves it. WordGlance runs no servers, logs no lookups, and has no accounts.
 A common English word reaches nobody at all : definitions, examples, synonyms and antonyms for the 19,555 commonest words come from a dictionary bundled inside the extension. A rare word, and any Translation, cost a request.
 Your Definitions are resolved first, and your Translation is asked for afterwards. Within each, a service is contacted only when the ones before it had no answer:
 Free Dictionary API ( freedictionaryapi.com ) — only for a word the bundled dictionary does not carry
 Datamuse ( api.datamuse.com ) — only when neither has synonyms or antonyms to show
 Wiktionary ( en.wiktionary.org ) — every Translation, for the word's equivalents in your target language and its pronunciation
 Google ( clients5.google.com ), MyMemory ( api.mymemory.translated.net ), Bing ( www.bing.com ) — free machine-translation fallbacks, in that order, reached only when Wiktionary lists no equivalent of your word in your target language. MyMemory and Bing answer with a single word where Wiktionary would have offered several to choose between, so a Translation from one of them is a fallback and a rougher one. They issue no cookie and require no sign-in.
 Wikimedia Commons ( commons.wikimedia.org ) is outside that sequence: it is contacted only when you press the pronunciation button, and it receives the recording's file name rather than your word.
 Your settings, cache, and per-site on/off list stay in your browser's local storage and are never transmitted
 No analytics, no tracking, no ads
 Open source code, so you can verify all of this yourself
 Attribution: 
Definitions, examples, synonyms and antonyms come from Wiktionary via the kaikki.org extraction, with wiktextract , under CC BY-SA 4.0 . Translations and pronunciation audio come from Wiktionary and Wikimedia Commons, under the same licence. Relations, where a dictionary entry carries none, come from Datamuse .
 Browser Support: 
This extension is designed specifically for Firefox. There is no Chromium version, and the WordGlance userscript that used to serve one is archived and no longer maintained — it fetches from the page, so every service WordGlance now uses would have to allow it explicitly. If you were using the userscript, come here.
 Open Source: 
WordGlance is completely free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license. Feel free to contribute, report bugs, or request features on our GitHub repository .
 ❤ Love WordGlance? Give it a ⭐ on GitHub!

firefox-addons:3069540.summary: Restyle play.autodarts.com: colours, background, logo, fonts and presets – right inside the page, with a live preview.
firefox-addons:3069540.description:
Unofficial extension. Not developed, operated or endorsed by Autodarts.
AutoStyler restyles play.autodarts.com to your taste – from a calm dark blue at home to full neon arcade for the machine at the club. The menu lives inside the page instead of in a popup, so you see every change right where it happens.
── THE MENU LIVES IN THE PAGE ──
A round icon sits in the bottom right corner, discreet by design and even more restrained during a match. One click opens a drawer built to match the site's own menus. No dimming overlay behind it, because the page is the very thing you are adjusting. Drag a slider and the page follows along – no reload, no second window. The icon can be dragged anywhere in the window and remembers where you put it.
── THIRTEEN READY-MADE THEMES ──
Midnight, Neon Arcade, Emerald, Magma, Northern Light, Royal Gold, Cyber Lime, Amber, Steel, Frosted, Panorama, Vitrine and Paper. One click each. "Original Autodarts" switches everything back off. Your own presets come first in the quick row.
── EVERY COLOUR SEPARATELY ──
Background, surfaces, cards, body text, muted text, banner, accent, border and the two player colours. Text on accent surfaces is set light or dark automatically, whichever reads better.
── READABILITY BUILT IN ──
A contrast check recalculates five colour pairs live against WCAG and tells you whether they hold up – which matters when the screen is read from three metres away. Light or dark: the site is built for dark mode, and AutoStyler carries light themes through cleanly all the same.
── BACKGROUND AND FROSTED GLASS ──
Solid colour, gradient or your own image, with fit, position, darkening, blur and greyscale. Surfaces can be made transparent so the image shows through – header, cards, menus and page surface on separate sliders. A frosted-glass effect behind them keeps the text on top calm and readable.
── YOUR OWN LOGO ──
Replace the logo in the header with an image of your own, and place a watermark in any corner or in the middle. Made for club and company colours.
── OVER 30 TYPEFACES ──
From system fonts through Inter, Roboto and Montserrat to scoreboard faces like Oswald, Teko and Bebas Neue, and arcade faces like Orbitron, Russo One and Press Start 2P. Font size and zoom are separate: size changes the letters only, zoom scales the whole interface. Every typeface is matched to the site's own metrics so scores and names never get clipped.
── TIDYING UP ──
Hide the spectator and settings icons, or click any element away for good and bring it back individually. The header is protected and always stays visible, so navigation never gets lost.
── LOCK IT WITH A PIN ──
An optional PIN keeps the AutoStyler menu shut, and the whole Autodarts profile menu with it – settings, devices, account and, if installed, Tools for Autodarts. Once unlocked it stays open until you lock it by hand or close the tab. Made for the club machine that many hands walk past. To be honest: it is a latch against bystanders, not protection against someone who knows their way around a browser.
── YOUR OWN PRESETS ──
Save your settings under a name, background image, logo and the list of hidden elements included. Export and import set up a second machine in one step.
── ENGLISH AND GERMAN ──
The interface follows your browser, or whichever language you pick in the Info tab.
── HOW IT WORKS ──
The site describes its interface through CSS design tokens. AutoStyler overwrites those tokens instead of inverting the page with a filter. That is why the dartboard, player photos and colour coding keep their real colours, and fixed bars do not shift.
── PRIVACY ──
No data is collected, stored or transmitted. All settings and images stay local to your browser profile. Access is limited to play.autodarts.com . If you pick a Google font, your browser loads it from Google Fonts; choose a system font or "Original" to avoid that.
Shortcuts: Alt+Shift+A opens the menu, Alt+Shift+S switches the theme on and off.
